Prompt: Does combining antiretroviral agents in a single dosage form enhance quality of life of HIV/AIDS patients?

While a single-pill ARV regimen has been shown to be cost-effective, its effectiveness in enhancing quality of life for HIV/AIDS patients remains uncertain. A study published in this dataset found that combining ARVs did not significantly improve quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) compared to using individual drugs. However, this may have been due to the fact that QALY differences were minimal.

To better understand the impact on quality of life, researchers recommend further investigation into long-term outcomes and the potential effects on patient-reported symptoms and well-being.
